pr_title: Comprehensive workflow reminder management for booking lifecycle events

validations.droid_claim:
[P1] One cancellation failure prevents deleting any cancelled reminders

The try/catch wraps the entire cancellation loop and the final `Promise.all`. If a single `client.request` throws (transient SendGrid/network error), the code jumps to catch and none of the queued `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` operations run, leaving already-cancelled reminders in the DB and retried every run. Handle errors per-reminder (or ensure deletes for successful cancellations run even if one cancellation fails) so partial failures don’t block cleanup.
validations.impact: A transient SendGrid error on any single reminder cancellation aborts the entire loop, leaving already-successfully-cancelled reminders in the DB. These orphaned rows will be retried on every cron run indefinitely.
validations.reasoning: Lines 53-76: The try block wraps the entire `for...of` loop and the final `Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)`. The loop sequentially calls `client.request()` for each reminder, then pushes a prisma delete to the array. If `client.request` throws on reminder N, execution jumps to the catch block and the `Promise.all` for all previously-queued deletes (reminders 1..N-1) never executes. Those reminders were already cancelled in SendGrid but their DB rows persist with `cancelled: true`, causing them to be re-fetched and re-cancelled on every subsequent cron invocation.

validations.droid_claim:
[P0] immediateDelete cancels SendGrid but leaves reminder row unchanged

When `immediateDelete` is true, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` cancels the SendGrid scheduled send and then returns without updating/deleting the corresponding `WorkflowReminder` row. Call sites use `immediateDelete` (e.g. workflow deletion / booking reschedule) and no longer delete reminders in Prisma, so this can leave reminders looking still `scheduled` and never eligible for the `cancelled` cleanup path. Consider deleting the row (or at least setting `cancelled=true`) in the `immediateDelete` branch as well.
validations.impact: When a booking is rescheduled (handleNewBooking.ts), old reminders are cancelled in SendGrid via immediateDelete but the DB rows remain with scheduled=true and cancelled=null. These orphaned rows are never cleaned up by the cron job (which only targets cancelled=true rows) and persist indefinitely.
validations.reasoning: The `immediateDelete` branch in deleteScheduledEmailReminder (lines 218-225) cancels the SendGrid batch but returns without touching the DB row. For the workflow-delete and step-delete call sites, this is mitigated by Prisma cascade deletes (WorkflowStep -> WorkflowReminder onDelete: Cascade). However, in handleNewBooking.ts (reschedule path), the old booking is NOT deleted — it's kept with status changes — so no cascade occurs. The WorkflowReminder rows for the old booking remain in the DB with scheduled=true, cancelled=null/false, creating orphaned records that the cron cleanup in scheduleEmailReminders.ts never targets (it only queries cancelled=true).

validations.droid_claim:
[P1] Unawaited async work in forEach when cancelling edited-step reminders

`remindersToUpdate.forEach(async (reminder) => { ... })` starts async cancellation/update work but nothing awaits these promises. In serverless/request-scoped execution this can race with subsequent scheduling/response completion, leaving old reminders not reliably cancelled. Use `await Promise.all(remindersToUpdate.map(...))` (or a `for...of` with `await`) to ensure cancellations complete deterministically.
validations.impact: When workflow steps are edited, old reminder cancellations fire-and-forget. In serverless environments the function may return before cancellations complete, leaving old SendGrid scheduled sends active and stale DB rows. Subsequent scheduling of new reminders races with incomplete cancellations.
validations.reasoning: The `remindersToUpdate.forEach(async (reminder) => {...})` pattern on line ~574 launches async operations (deleteScheduledEmailReminder which calls SendGrid API and/or Prisma) but forEach ignores the returned promises. The enclosing mutation continues immediately to schedule new reminders and return to the client. This is a well-known anti-pattern in JavaScript — forEach does not await async callbacks. The same pattern also appears in multiple other places in this file (workflow delete, step delete, new event type scheduling), compounding the issue.
